book_title: The Sealed Garden Opens: The Kephalaia's Seven States of Regeneration
structural_overview: The book is the regeneration cycle in seven movements, each section corresponding precisely to one of the seven states the Song of Solomon and the Kephalaia substrate independently narrate. The proportions are themselves the architecture: Section 1 stands alone (1 teaching, 1 chapter) — the threshold awakening, the eyes opening within the molded vessel. Section 2 is long expository seeking (17 teachings, 8 chapters) — the soul going through the streets of the city, mapping the structures of doctrine the watchmen represent. Section 3 is brief and intense (4 teachings, 2 chapters) — the sealed garden opens, the Beloved is in his garden; the Lord at his inmost is named, the Land of Light entered, the eternity of what is given confessed. Section 4 is the longest section (28 teachings, 10 chapters) — the alternation of states, the deeper work the first conjunction has exposed: the self's auto-genesis, the watchmen now wounding, the soul bound in the twelve members, the three malformations and their cleansing. Section 5 is the parallel survey (23 teachings, 8 chapters) — the same divine outgoing now reviewed in its growth, the wheel turning peacefully through the heavens, the cosmic body and the inward gathering. Section 6 is the second culmination (26 teachings, 9 chapters) — the kiss without shame, the daily purification, the Virgin and Continent, the three forms in the perfect man, the full integration achieved at a depth State 3 could not reach. Section 7 is the coda (5 teachings, 3 chapters) — the seal upon the heart and the arm, the prayer that bears the whole, the two essences forever distinguished, the Yes and Amen identified. The book's central architectural feature: two long sections (4 and 6) flanking two brief peaks (3 and 7), with two transitional sections (2 and 5) carrying the soul between the wounds and the sealings. This is exactly the alternation pattern the thesis identifies as the signature of genuine regeneration narrative — and it is here found at the macro scale of the entire corpus.
reading_order_note: The corpus order is preserved exactly. The 104 teachings are read in their original sequence, and the seven section boundaries fall at the precise teaching numbers the application block specifies (T1; T2-T18; T19-T22; T23-T50; T51-T73; T74-T99; T100-T104). No teaching has been moved, excluded, or grouped against the corpus's own ordering. The natural fit between teaching content and seven-state arc constitutes independent confirmation of the thesis: the Kephalaia substrate is itself a passage through the seven states at the macro scale, not a static catalogue but a regeneration cycle that unfolds in reading order. The corpus does not need rearrangement because the corpus is itself the cycle.

observations.title: The Two Long Sections Flank the Two Brief Peaks
observations.content: Sections 4 and 6 are the two longest in the book (28 and 26 teachings). They flank Sections 3 and 7, which are the two brief, intense peaks (4 and 5 teachings). This is not editorial accident; it is the alternation-of-states pattern at the macro scale. Section 3 is the first conjunction (entry into the inmost), brief because the inmost cannot be elaborated; Section 4 is the long deeper work that the first conjunction has exposed; Section 6 is the second, fuller conjunction; Section 7 is the brief permanent seal. The corpus enacts at scale what the Song narrates in eight verses (5:2-8): conjunction, withdrawal, deeper work, deeper conjunction, permanent sealing.

observations.title: Two Macro-Redemptive Narratives at T15 and T100
observations.content: T15 (Twelve Greatnesses descending to Adam) is the longest single teaching of Section 2. T100 (First Man's prayer in distress) is the longest single teaching of Section 7. Both narrate the entire redemptive descent and ascent — but from different vantages. T15 narrates from outside, in the Silver Church register: the cosmological architecture of the descent from the hidden Father through the Mother of Life, First Man, Living Spirit, Third Ambassador, Jesus the Radiance, down to Adam and home in the Last Andrias. T100 narrates from inside, as prayer: the cry from affliction, the petition, the powers sent, the conjunction sealed. The same cycle perceived through truth (T15) and through good (T100), each placed exactly where the seven-state arc requires it: the cosmic descent at the end of seeking, the soul-level prayer at the seal.

observations.title: The Two-Essences Frame Opens and Closes the Book
observations.content: T2 (Two Trees) at the start of Section 2 establishes the foundational dualism the seeker must first recognize: life and death as two trees with corresponding members, one rational faculty in five degrees met by the same five turned the other way. T103 (Two Essences) at the end of Section 7 closes the same dyad: 'Two substances are those existing from the beginning: the Light and the Darkness, the beautiful and the bitter one and the life and the death.' The dualism opens the seeking and closes the seal. What State 1 only opens the eyes to see, State 7 finally and forever distinguishes — the beautiful separated forth from the darkness, no waters able to mingle them again.

observations.title: The Watchmen Pattern: Same Doctrine, Different Wound
observations.content: The teachings that lay out the structure of divine outgoing in Section 2 (the 'watchmen' the seeker meets in the city) — the four days, five faces, twelve greatnesses, three times, four wars, four salvations — are paralleled by structurally identical teachings in Section 4: the twelve judges (T28), twelve thrones (T29), three days and two deaths (T41), three plagues (T43), four ages of separation (T48). The same architecture that guided in State 2 now wounds in State 4, exactly as the Song's watchmen 'go about the city' first finding (3:3) and later wounding (5:7). The corpus recognizes this and treats the doctrinal architecture twice — once as map for the seeker, once as instrument of the deeper discrimination.

observations.title: The Five-Faculty Structure as Deepest Substrate
observations.content: Across all seven sections, one substrate holds: the rational in five degrees (mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection). The Two Trees (T2) map life and death through these five members. The Five Faces (T5), Five Fathers (T7), Five Mysteries (T9), Five Awakeners (T13), Five Sons of First Man (T15), Five Forms of Darkness (T27), Five Living Fires (T75), Five Mysteries of First Man again (T94), Five Births of the Body (T90), the fivefold cosmos that cannot stand if one degree is missing (T97), and the five-articulating-degrees by which the word becomes audible (T92) — all draw on the same fivefold articulation. This is not redundancy; it is the corpus showing one ontological structure recognized at every register where it appears. The five-faculty pattern is what the soul is, what it traverses, and what it returns to.

observations.title: Compassions and Weepings as Sign of the Cycle's Reality
observations.content: T59 (Three Griefs of Mother of Life) and T60 (Four Weepings of First Man's Garments) are placed in Section 5, the Garden Inspected. They are not lamentations of failure; they are the recognition that the regeneration cycle costs at every register. The Lord, going forth, weeps three times in descent under necessity (knowing what the self will do) and a fourth time at the consummation, mourning those who prepared themselves for falsity. The three compassions and four weepings are signs that the cycle is real and not theoretical: the divine outgoing actually grieves. State 5's inspection of growth includes the inspection of what was sorrowful in the doing of it.

observations.title: Damaged Teachings Carry the Sealing Function
observations.content: Several teachings near the corpus's close are heavily fragmentary — T95 (hidden things in the eye), T102 (mystical seeing), T104 (cherubim, pillars, garments). The damage does not weaken the book; it confirms it. State 7 is the seal, and the seal is not narrative — it is stamp, imprint, fixed character. What survives in T102 and T104 carries the doctrinal close exactly: the Yes and Amen identified as Calling and Hearing, the supports of the regenerated rational named, the inner sight opened in the soul's appointed time. The Song's State 7 likewise closes not in narrative but in declarative imprint: 'Set me as a seal... love is strong as death... many waters cannot quench love.' The corpus and the Song agree on form as well as content: the seal is given, not narrated.
